The Gap
Missing teeth change more than your smile. They change what you eat, how you speak, and the shape of your jaw.
Your teeth move when you eat
Teeth that shift or feel loose make chewing unpredictable, and the foods you avoid keep adding up.
You cover your mouth when you laugh
Hiding your smile in photos and conversations is exhausting, and it rarely stays at the mouth.
Your dentures need adhesive to stay in
Messy adhesives, dietary restrictions, and the constant background worry that something slips.
Your jaw has started to change shape
Missing roots let the jawbone recede. Implants fuse to the bone and stop that drift.
Find out if you're a candidate
Free consultation · 3D scan · a written plan
The Anatomy
Three parts that behave like a real tooth

A dental implant has a titanium or zirconium post that sits in your jawbone the way a tooth root does, an abutment on top of it, and the crown that attaches to the abutment. In the weeks after surgery the post fuses with the bone, which is what makes the result stable rather than merely attached.
The post
Placed into the jawbone using fully guided All-on-X technique, for accuracy and precision.
The abutment
Seats on the post once it has integrated, and carries the tooth above it.
The crown
Matched to your face, skin tone and gum line, and finished in the practice's own lab.
Illustration, not a patient photograph. Planning is done on a 3D scan before surgery — digitally, rather than in the chair.
The Options
Four ways to replace what's missing
Which one is right depends on how many teeth are gone and how much bone is left to work with. That is what the consultation is for.
Single tooth implant
Replaces one tooth without touching the healthy teeth on either side, and stops the shifting that follows a gap.
Multiple teeth
Bridges and crowns supported by implants — no adhesives and none of the dietary restrictions that come with partial dentures.
Implant-supported denture
Attaches to surgically placed posts, so it holds far better than a conventional denture.
Full arch (All-on-X)
A whole new set of teeth on four or more implants — often placed the same day as surgery.

The Surgeon
Every phase of your case, one surgeon

Dr. Bennett founded Arvada Dental Center and has practised in Colorado for almost twenty years. He oversees every phase of an implant case himself — the planning, the surgery, the sedation and the lab work — which is why you are not handed between offices halfway through.
Doctorate of Dental Surgery, University of Iowa, 2001
Thousands of implants placed and restored
Board certified to administer IV sedation
Immersive dental surgery training every year
The Path
From first call to new teeth.
Free consultation and 3D scan
Dr. Bennett examines you, scans the jaw, and tells you what is actually possible — including when an implant is not the right answer. You leave with a written plan and a real number.
Placement, with sedation if you want it
The posts are placed using fully guided technique. Most patients choose IV sedation, which Dr. Bennett administers himself.
Healing and integration
The implants fuse with the jawbone over the following weeks. On full-arch cases you go home with fixed teeth the same day rather than waiting it out.
Final restoration
Your permanent crowns or arch go on, matched to your face, skin tone and gum line, and finished in the practice's own lab.

The things people ask first

Age on its own is rarely the deciding factor — bone volume and general health matter far more. That is exactly what the 3D scan at your free consultation is for, and Dr. Bennett will tell you plainly if implants are not the right route for you.
Dr. Bennett is board certified to administer IV sedation and does so himself. Most implant patients at the practice choose it, and the procedure is carried out with you fully comfortable.

It depends on the case. Full-arch patients frequently leave with fixed teeth on the day of surgery, then return for the final restoration once the implants have integrated with the bone. Single-tooth cases follow the same pattern over a shorter span.
